params.body:
## Symptom

Production, maintenance mode with the admin bypass cookie: `GET /showroomaffiche?ids=[22825]` answered a nginx **502 Bad Gateway** with nothing in `laravel.log`.

## Cause

The poster (`AfficheController::index`, TCPDF `writeHTML`) gave TCPDF the site's own URLs for the photos (`stocklist.index.image`) and the dealer logo (`dealer.index.image`); the sales agreement footer (`ExportController`, `$pdf->Image(LinkHelper::route(...))`) and the loan form's first damage photo did the same. TCPDF fetches such a URL itself, so the server called its own public address to read a file it stores. In maintenance mode that address returns the 503 page (the bypass cookie is not sent on a server-side call); with three photos and default timeouts PHP-FPM outlived `fastcgi_read_timeout` and nginx answered 502. Outside maintenance the loopback was just as fragile (DNS, TLS, the same FPM pool serving itself), and on staging `Outbound::seal()` already blocked it with a 500.

## Fix

- `App\Support\PdfImage` reads vehicle photos through `VehicleImageService::getImageBinary`, the code behind the endpoint, so the PDF gets exactly the bytes the URL would have returned: the derived size (`sm`/`md`) from the bucket when it exists, built and stored otherwise, the original untouched. Other disks (`dealers`) are read raw.
- `PdfImage::vehicle()` / `PdfImage::src()` return the TCPDF `@base64` source and fall back to `default_vehicle.png` when a photo is missing; when even that is missing the tag is left out. One missing photo never kills the PDF.
- One time budget per PDF (`BUDGET_SECONDS = 20`): once spent, the remaining photos get the placeholder instead of waiting on a slow bucket.
- `showroom/partials/fallback_photos.blade.php`, `showroom/partials/dealer_client_info.blade.php`, `offertes/_tabs_bruikleen/damage.blade.php` and the three `ExportController` footers use it; no PDF template or controller builds an image URL any more (a test greps for `(stocklist|ownvehicle|dealer).index.image` in them).
- The `!config('app.debug')` guard that hid the poster photos locally (because `artisan serve` cannot call itself) is removed: there is nothing left to call.

## Also: the PDF controllers return a response

`AfficheController` (poster, energy card) and `ExportController` (agreement, borderel, winner print) ended in TCPDF `Output($name, 'I')`: TCPDF echoed the bytes and sent its own headers, the controller returned nothing. No difference for the browser, but middleware saw an empty response and the poster test from PR 416 flooded the phpunit console with the raw PDF. `App\Support\PdfResponse::inline(PDF::Output('', 'S'), $filename)` now returns the document with the same inline headers (`Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename=...`); the tests assert on the response content instead of `expectOutputRegex`. The order/offer/rental PDFs still echo; not touched here.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/PdfImageReadsDirectlyTest.php` (new): same bytes as the endpoint for `orig`/`sm`/`md` on a fake `vehicles` disk; a missing file yields the placeholder and never an exception; other disks read raw; no template points TCPDF at the site's URL; the poster route renders `%PDF-1.` for a vehicle with three photos (one missing on disk) and a dealer logo with `Http::fake()` + `assertNothingSent()`. `ShowroomPosterWarningTest` (PR 416) now also asserts no HTTP request leaves during the poster.

Rule **R S2-8.12** in `12-s2-eigen-wagenpark-publiceren.md`; finding `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/2026-09-15-affiche-502-eigen-url.md` (ernst nu, opgelost).

`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'Pdf|Affiche|Showroom|Agreement|Borderel|Image|RulesCoverage|RulesIdentity|CompiledViews|Smoke'`: OK (320 tests, 801 assertions), no PDF bytes on the console.

Supersedes #428 (same branch, before the response change).

## Open

The mail templates (`mails/export_vehicle.blade.php` and co) also link to `stocklist.index.image`, but there the recipient's mail client loads the photo, not the server; not a loopback, left as is.
params.title: PDFs read their photos directly instead of calling the site
